thm:aomega-fourone-dt-count:
Theorem The figure-eight Stokes integer A_\omega(4_1) = 3 is a BPS/DT count (conditional on the Stokes--DT--BPS bridge). Conditional on Resurgent Stokes constants are Donaldson--Thomas / BPS degeneracies. Under the closed-sector Stokes--DT--BPS bridge, the G3 Stokes integer of the figure-eight 4_1 is a BPS/DT count:

  A_\omega(4_1) \;=\; \dim \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{BPS}}\big(T[4_1]\big) \;=\; 3 .
prop:dt-spectrum-bar-eigenspace:
Proposition The DT-spectrum split is the bar-eigenspace decomposition of the q\to0 Stokes constants. Let (\mathfrak{d}^+, \mathfrak{d}^-) = (4, 3) be the ordered pair of certified q\to0 Stokes constants of the figure-eight's chiral partner 5_2 (the (96)/(97) factorization constants of S^+(0), S^-(0); both integer, GGM eq 98). Under the chirality involution \tau — the q\mapsto q^{-1} mirror swap (\mathfrak{d}^+,\mathfrak{d}^-)\mapsto(\mathfrak{d}^-,\mathfrak{d}^+) — the pair carries a faithful \mathbb{Z}/2 grading into a bar-even and a bar-odd part,

  \mathrm{even} = \mathfrak{d}^+ + \mathfrak{d}^- = 7 \quad(\tau\text{-fixed}),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{odd} = \mathfrak{d}^+ - \mathfrak{d}^- = 1 \quad(\tau\text{-negated}),

with faithful reconstruction 2\mathfrak{d}^\pm = \mathrm{even} \pm \mathrm{odd}. The bar-odd part is nonzero, so no \tau-symmetric scalar recovers the ordered datum; for the amphichiral 4_1 the bar-odd part vanishes and the spectrum degenerates to a single constant.

This is the base brick (milestone M0) of the categorical Route C for the figure-eight monodromy datum A_\omega. The scalar exclusion — no single-valued Wedderburn Euler characteristic, recursion order, block count, or A-polynomial L-degree equals the 5_2 DT datum — is a negative statement. The bar-eigenspace decomposition converts it into a positive one: the DT count is not a number but a \mathbb{Z}/2-graded (bar-even \oplus bar-odd) object, of which a scalar is the \tau-trivial shadow. "No scalar serves the datum" is exactly "the bar-odd part is nonzero", which for the chiral 5_2 it is (=1) and for the amphichiral 4_1 it is not (=0).

The grading is the q\mapsto q^{-1} bar-involution that runs through the whole even/odd programme; the chirality-refined, set-valued count the exclusion forces is therefore the categorification of that involution's eigenspaces, not a generic cohomological-Hall computation. Milestone M2 supplies a structural characterization of the putative closed-sector BPS spectrum — not a construction of it: taking the certified eq-(98) constants as Donaldson–Thomas invariants (conditional on the DT/BPS bridge), every Borel ray is distinct, so the Davison–Meinhardt plethystic log is trivial and \dim \mathrm{BPS}_d = |\Omega_d| with no superpotential and no motivic q-correction — the spectrum would be abelian, which is why A_\omega and the whole Stokes tower are integers rather than Poincaré polynomials . This does not build the closed-sector quiver-with-potential (Q,W) (Milestone M1, still unwritten), does not compute a cohomology from a category, and does not derive A_\omega: the count is imported (conditional on the bridge above), and what M2 adds is only that its BPS realization would carry no hidden motivic multiplicity. The Hecke-to-BPS bridge (M3) that would derive rather than import the count stays open; this proposition fixes only the structural target. The onward identification of A_\omega with the bar-odd decay leak S has no literature support and is not derivable; it is not carried here.
prop:schur-weyl-mass-decomposition:
Proposition Schur–Weyl decomposition of the atomic mass trace. The Markov trace of the atomic braid \mathcal{A} \in H_{3A}(q) decomposes over partitions \lambda \vdash 3A as:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{A})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, 3A}
    \frac{s_\lambda(\mathbf{q})}{H_q(\lambda)}
    \cdot
    \chi^\lambda(\mathcal{A})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, 3A} w_\lambda(q)\, \mathrm{tr}_\lambda,

where s_\lambda is the Schur function, H_q(\lambda) is the q-hook product, and \chi^\lambda is the Specht-module character.

For a single nucleon (A=1), the H_3(q) partitions \{(3), (2,1), (1,1,1)\} correspond to the symmetric, standard, and antisymmetric Wedderburn blocks. The w_\lambda weights recover the three-parameter Wedderburn mass formula precisely.

The additive-Wedderburn approximation sums the A=1 weights over each generator of the A-nucleon braid. This approximation discards all partitions with rows longer than 3, corresponding to inter-nucleon entanglement. For light atoms, the discarded weights remain negligible. For A \ge 6, the excluded boundary partitions \lambda = (3A-1, 1) and pair partitions \lambda = (3A-2, 2) accumulate massive q-hook products, causing the observed 5\%--20\% binding-energy drift in the approximation.

Schur-Weyl duality isolates the physical origin of each correction into specific partition geometries. The base volume derives from the symmetric partition (3A). The surface correction derives from the boundary partition (3A-1, 1). The pair-crossing interaction derives from the (3A-2, 2) pair partition. Magic shell-closure peaks derive from sharp hook-product factorization at rectangular partitions.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It applies q-deformation identities over an abstract coefficient ring and specializes them to real-valued physical observables at q_0.
rem:categorical-mass-positivity:
Remark Structural positivity of categorical mass and action. The categorical mass evaluates the observation functor \tau on graded projective KLR modules. The functor takes the graded Euler characteristic, rendering each coefficient the non-negative integer dimension of a \mathrm{Hom}-space:

  [\tau(\mathfrak{M}_K)]_d \;=\;
  \dim_R \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{K}_n}\bigl(P_d, \mathfrak{M}_K\bigr)
  \;\in\; \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}.

The polynomial \tau(\mathfrak{M}_K) is the mass-spectrum generating function. Each coefficient corresponds to the microstate degeneracy of a graded Hecke energy level. The resulting mass formula remains structurally positive by categorical definition.
rem:mass-spectrum-generating-function:
Remark Confined Laurent polynomial P_K(q) as mass-spectrum generating function: functorial equivalence to scalar mass via substrate evaluation. The polynomial P_K(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] is a graded Euler characteristic, not a macroscopic mass scalar. The two link via a functorial composition that evaluates the generating function at the substrate parameter q_0.

Each term c_d q^d of P_K(q) parses as a mass component. The exponent d measures the graded Hecke energy, tracking the internal topological tension. The coefficient c_d counts the microstate degeneracy, tallying the orthogonal Hom-channels at that energy. The full polynomial constitutes the partition function over the internal homological slices.

Evaluating this polynomial at q_0 recovers the macroscopic mass:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{K}}
  \;\approx\;
  m_0 \cdot \bigl|P_K(q_0)\bigr|.

Equating the polynomial directly to the scalar erases both the microstate spectrum and the substrate dependence, discarding the specific data governing branching ratios and resonance widths.
prop:graded-markov-trace-from-gs-filtrat:
Proposition Graded Markov trace as the induced trace on J^\ell / J^{\ell+1}. For each \ell \in \mathbb{N} there is a uniquely determined \mathbb{Q}(q)-linear trace

  \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}
  \;:\;
  J^\ell / J^{\ell+1}
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathbb{Q}(q)

that agrees with the restriction of \mathrm{tr}_M on J^\ell and vanishes entirely on the lower stratum J^{\ell+1}.

The standard Markov trace descends constructively along the Gröbner-Shirshov filtration quotient. The formulation automatically secures compatibility with the spectral sequence and forces vanishing above the confinement level. The construction replaces the opaque analytic assumption with a strict algebraic descent.
prop:residue-at-root:
Proposition Cyclotomic residues of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} — algebraic definition. Let T_w \in J^\ell / J^{\ell+1} have \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) \in \mathbb{Q}(q), and suppose \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) lies in the Habiro completion \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. The cyclotomic residue

  \mathrm{Res}_{q \to \zeta_\ell}(\Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell})(T_w)

is the image of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) under the cyclotomic projection

  \pi_{n_\ell}
  \;:\;
  \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}
  \longrightarrow
  \mathbb{Z}[q] / \Phi_{n_\ell}(q),

evaluating identically within the residue field \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_\ell).

The cyclotomic residue is defined purely algebraically within the Habiro completion of \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. It avoids complex-analytic limits entirely. The formulation keeps the algebraic sector strictly within \mathbb{Q}-coefficients, fulfilling the three-calibration discipline.

The cyclotomic projection \pi_n is constructed: \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} is the ring of compatible threads in \mathbb{Z}[q]/(q;q)_N, N \ge 0, and \pi_n reads off the level-n class and reduces it modulo \Phi_n(q), which divides 1 - q^n and hence (q;q)_n. It is a ring homomorphism, and on a polynomial it is reduction modulo \Phi_n(q). The residue of a product is therefore the product of the residues.

The hypothesis that \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) lies in \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} is not proved here. That membership, together with the reality of the residue and its dependence only on the class of T_w modulo J^{\ell+1}(q), is the open content of Existence of the cyclotomic residue at each filtration level.
prf:residue-at-root:
Proof Proof of residue at root. The Habiro completion \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} is realised as the ring of threads (x_N)_{N \ge 0}, x_N \in \mathbb{Z}[q]/(q;q)_N with (q;q)_N = \prod_{k=1}^{N}(1 - q^k), compatible under the reductions \mathbb{Z}[q]/(q;q)_M \to \mathbb{Z}[q]/(q;q)_N for N \le M. These reductions exist because (q;q)_N divides (q;q)_M. Compatibility is preserved by sums and products, so the threads form a subring of the product.

For n \ge 1 the cyclotomic polynomial \Phi_n(q) divides 1 - q^n, which is a factor of (q;q)_n. Reduction modulo \Phi_n(q) therefore factors through \mathbb{Z}[q]/(q;q)_n, and

  \pi_n(x) \;:=\; x_n \bmod \Phi_n(q)
  \;\in\; \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_n(q)

defines a ring homomorphism \pi_n : \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_n(q). On the constant thread of a polynomial p, \pi_n returns the class of p, so \pi_n is surjective and restricts to the usual reduction on \mathbb{Z}[q].

By hypothesis, \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) is an element of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. Applying \pi_{n_\ell} and identifying \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_{n_\ell}(q) with \mathbb{Z}[\zeta_\ell] gives the residue, an element of the cyclotomic ring. Because \pi_{n_\ell} is a ring homomorphism, the residue of a sum or product is the sum or product of the residues. \blacksquare

The construction does not use analytic continuation. Habiro shows that, for elements of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}, these projections agree with evaluation at roots of unity [habiro2004, §1.2]; that comparison is not needed for the statement.
prf:graded-markov-trace-from-gs-filtrati:
Proof Proof of graded markov trace from gs filtration. Sketch.

The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M is uniquely characterised by its cyclicity and Markov property (Existence and non-degeneracy of the Markov trace (Jones, 1987)). The GS filtration J^\bullet is two-sided [geckpfeiffer2000, mathas1999], so for T_1 \in J^a, T_2 \in J^b, T_1 T_2 \in J^{a+b}. Cyclicity then implies that \mathrm{tr}_M(T_1 T_2) - \mathrm{tr}_M(T_2 T_1) = 0 \in \mathbb{Q}(q)_{a + b}, which is the right-hand grading at the correct level. Hence the restriction of \mathrm{tr}_M to J^\ell descends to J^\ell / J^{\ell+1} (any T \in J^{\ell+1} has \mathrm{tr}_M(T) \in \mathbb{Q}(q)_{\ell+1}, which is strictly above the level \ell). Uniqueness follows from the universal property of the quotient.

The construction is purely algebraic — it makes no reference to analytic continuation, complex evaluation, or roots of unity. The companion block Cyclotomic residues of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} — algebraic definition supplies the algebraic definition of the residues required to assemble the GB-residue spectral sum (Length-filtration spectral sequence of the Hochschild complex of H_n(R, q)).
prop:gb-residue-spectral-sum:
Proposition Gröbner–Shirshov residue spectral sum for the mass trace. For a closed braid knot with Hecke normal form T_w \in H_n(R, q), the categorical mass admits the symbolic decomposition:

  \mathfrak{m}_{q_0, \mathcal{K}}
  \;=\;
  \bigl|\int_A T_w(q_0)\bigr|
  \;+\;
  \sum_{\ell = 1}^{\ell(\mathcal{K}, q_0)}
    r_\ell(T_w; q_0),
  \qquad
  r_\ell(T_w; q_0)
    \;=\;
    \frac{\mathrm{Res}_{q = \zeta_\ell}\!
      \bigl[\Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M,\ell}(T_w)\bigr]}
    {q_0 - \zeta_\ell}.

The numerators are the stratum residues feeding the cyclotomic coefficients a_m of the Habiro expansion.

The confinement filtration makes H_n(R, q) a filtered differential algebra. The residue r_\ell(T_w; q_0) is the pairing of the trace integral with the level-\ell filtration stratum. The sum evaluated across all strata constructs the total mass.

The Cauchy-kernel factor 1/(q_0 - \zeta_\ell) is a formal symbol. The expression is an identity in the Grothendieck group of the filtered algebra, not a convergent complex-analytic equality. The primitive roots of unity densely pack S^1, destroying any meromorphic neighborhood. The Habiro cyclotomic completion supplies the rigorous convergent framework.

Under the fibre functor \tau, the categorical filtration stratum maps to the geometric jet bundle on the elliptic curve. The cyclotomic residues map to Picard-Lefschetz residues at the discriminant locus off S^1, forcing convergent evaluation on the archimedean side.
sec:phi-q-markov-residue-habiro-preamble:
When the resummed trace series is analytically continued across the z-Habiro ring, its behaviour at roots of unity is governed by cyclotomic residues. This section proves fixed-level pair equality and the uniform \Delta_{\max} jet-tower bound, and states the equivalence between the algebraic topological mass formula and the Habiro residue sum; the analytic identification of the residue contributions with the cyclotomic tail remains open, and machine-precision agreement on the available atomic Markov traces is the evidence for it. On each Hecke irreducible the same ladder factorises the Markov-traced character, conditional on the c_k recursion kernel.

Geometrically, each cyclotomic residue measures the braid holonomy around a singular Seifert fibre. Splitting the graded trace into its smooth polynomial part and its singular residue sum provides the categorical foundation for Strutinsky's nuclear shell-correction method, determines the full pole structure of the sixth-term binding density, and yields the categorical derivation of the Borromean h^4 = -3/4 coefficient together with the Pochhammer normalisation bridge.
lem:tower-pair-equality-fixed-level:
Lemma Pair-contribution equality at a fixed jet level: z^2 \sum_{(i,j) \in \mathcal{P}_n} \Phi_q(|\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}|) is an exact identity. Let n \in \mathbb{N} be a brane jet level and let \mathcal{P}_n = \{(i, j) : 0 \le i < j\} be the full set of unordered pair blow-up centres at level n. The pair contribution at level n equals:

  \mathrm{pairs}_n
  \;=\;
  z^2 \sum_{(i, j) \in \mathcal{P}_n}
    \Phi_q\!\bigl(\bigl|\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}\bigr|\bigr).

The formula is an exact equality, not an upper bound.

The prior upper-bound framing incorrectly assumed the pentagon inequality applied to scalar volumes. The true algebraic basis is the exact Markov-pair identity \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i \sigma_j) = z^2. Lifting this identity to the traced volumes preserves the strict equality at every jet level.
prf:tower-pair-equality-fixed-level:
Proof Proof of tower pair equality fixed level. By the Markov-trace factorization theorem (Exact factorization of the nuclear Markov trace), the level-n Markov trace of a product of factors decomposes as a sum over subset structures with weights determined by the Markov parameter z. For a pair (i, j) \in \mathcal{P}_n, the two-factor subset contributes the weight z^2 (from All-pairs Markov-trace identity \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z^2: \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i \sigma_j) = z \cdot z = z^2, adjacent or not). The dilogarithm \Phi_q applied to the absolute value of the pair product |\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}| is the quantum-dilogarithm regularization of the pair's contribution to the jet-tower mass.

Pair commutativity Pair commutation at the traced-volume level ensures the pair index (i, j) vs (j, i) does not double-count (the absolute value |\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}| = |\hat V_j^{(n)} \hat V_i^{(n)}| is symmetric). Summing over \mathcal{P}_n — the set of unordered pairs — gives the level-n pair contribution

  \mathrm{pairs}_n
  \;=\;
  z^2 \sum_{(i, j) \in \mathcal{P}_n}
    \Phi_q\!\bigl(\bigl|\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}\bigr|\bigr),

as an exact equality. \square
conj:jet-tower-uniform-delta-max:
Conjecture Uniform per-level binding bound |\Delta^{(n)}(\varrho)| \le \Delta_{\max}(\varrho) for the brane tower. For every confined vortex \varrho, there exists a finite real constant \Delta_{\max}(\varrho) < \infty bounding the per-level binding contribution:

  |\Delta^{(n)}(\varrho)| \;\le\; \Delta_{\max}(\varrho)
  \qquad\text{for all } n \ge 1.

The canonical formalism verifies this bound empirically at n = 1, 2, 3 for ^2\mathrm{H}, ^3\mathrm{H}, and ^3\mathrm{He}. The observed sequence decays geometrically by exactly \hbar_q^2, maintaining strict uniformity.

The geometric tail bound of the mass series relies conditionally on this conjecture. A proof cannot rest on E_2-collapse of the Gröbner–Shirshov spectral sequence, which fails for H_3. A Yekutieli categorical rigidity bound on the descent involution remains a candidate route.
rem:jet-tower-convergence-context:
Remark Boundedness hypothesis, engineering consequence, and confinement-SDP relation for jet-tower convergence. On the hypothesis.

The hypothesis |\Delta^{(n)}(\varrho)| \leq \Delta_{\max}(\varrho) — uniform boundedness of per-level binding across the brane tower — is the named conjecture uniform per-level binding bound. This proposition therefore reduces the convergence question to a single boundedness statement: once \Delta^{(n)} is shown to be bounded (uniformly or with growth slower than \hbar_q^{-2n}), the tail decays as a geometric series.

Empirically (see the canonical formalism and the formal derivation) the per-level terms for \mathrm{D}, \mathrm{T}, \mathrm{^{3}He} satisfy |\hbar_q^{2n} \Delta^{(n)}| \leq |\hbar_q^{2(n-1)} \Delta^{(n-1)}| \cdot \hbar_q^2 to three significant figures, and the uniform bound holds numerically for D, T, {}^{3}He across n = 1, \dots, 7 — consistent with \Delta^{(n)} being bounded (in fact roughly constant). Promoting that observation to a theorem closes the open subconjecture uniform per-level binding bound.
prop:full-pole-structure-mass-trace:
Proposition Cyclotomic expansion of the cleared mass trace. Let T_w \in H_n(q) be a standard basis element, with the Markov trace at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) and h = q - q^{-1}. Then:

  1. By the Hecke-algebra Markov-trace structure of V. F. R. Jones [jones1987], \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) is a polynomial in z of degree at most n-1 with coefficients in \mathbb{Z}[h]. Hence the cleared numerator
  N(T_w) \;:=\; (q^{2}+1)^{\,n-1}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) \;\in\; \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}].
  1. N(T_w) lies in the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} := \varprojlim_m \mathbb{Z}[q]/((q;q)_m) of Kazuo Habiro [habiro2004cyclotomic] (applied to unified Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants in [habiro2008]), in which q is a unit, and expands cyclotomically as
  N(T_w)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{m \geq 0} a_m(T_w)\,(q; q)_m .
  1. The trace itself is not in general an element of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. For T_w = \sigma_1 \in H_2(q), \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = z satisfies (1+q^{2})\,z = q^{3}, and evaluating at q = i (a ring map \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{Z}[i]) would give 0 = -i.

The primitive roots of unity populate S^1 densely, blocking any complex-analytic continuation across the boundary. The Habiro ring provides the algebraic substrate for the cleared numerator, not for the trace: the factor (q^{2}+1)^{-(n-1)} has poles at q = \pm i, and only after removing it does evaluation at every root of unity make sense.
prf:full-pole-structure-mass-trace:
Proof Proof of full pole structure mass trace. Part 1. Induct on n. On H_1(q) = R the trace is \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1. For w \in S_{n+1} \setminus S_n the coset decomposition gives T_w = T_u\,\sigma_n\,T_v with u, v \in S_n, so the Markov property and cyclicity give \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(T_v T_u). The product T_v T_u expands in the standard basis of H_n(q) with coefficients in \mathbb{Z}[h], because the only relation used is \sigma_i^{2} = h\,\sigma_i + 1. By induction each \mathrm{tr}_M(T_x), x \in S_n, is a polynomial in z of degree at most n-1 over \mathbb{Z}[h], so \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) has degree at most n. For w \in S_n the induction hypothesis applies directly. Since h \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] and (q^{2}+1)z = q^{3}, multiplying by (q^{2}+1)^{n-1} clears every denominator.

Part 2. \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm1}] \subset \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} because q is a unit there. Sequential division by (1 - q^{m+1}) produces the coefficients a_m (atomic Habiro expansion, Step 2) [habiro2004].

Part 3. Evaluation at a root of unity is a ring homomorphism on \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. If z lay in \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}, applying evaluation at q = i to (1+q^{2})z = q^{3} would give 0 = -i. \square
rem:full-pole-structure-mass-trace-inter: Remark The Mittag-Leffler residue sum as a heuristic shadow of the Habiro expansion. The earlier "\sum_{n,j} r_n^{(j)}/(q_0 - \zeta_n^{(j)})" expression is a formal residue spectral sum (GB residue spectral sum) — a heuristic shadow of the Habiro expansion valid only after one fixes a finite cyclotomic order and a regular evaluation point q_0 disjoint from S^1. It is not a convergent sum on or near S^1 and does not define \mathrm{tr}_M as a meromorphic function on \mathbb{C}. Each finite-order Cauchy-kernel partial sum is the q-adic image of a Habiro truncation; computational data confirms that for the proton and neutron the Cauchy kernel partial sum truncated at n \leq 6 is identically zero, in agreement with the cyclotomic expansion of the cleared numerator in the mass-trace pole structure (Cyclotomic expansion of the cleared mass trace) (the Habiro coefficients a_0, \ldots, a_5 vanish on the atomic trefoil class).
prf:habiro-expansion-atomic: Proof Proof of habiro expansion atomic. The proof is the constructive sequential cyclotomic-division algorithm. The general existence/uniqueness of the cyclotomic expansion (with a_m \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], no termination) is the content of (Habiro completion); the present proof specialises to atomic braids and establishes termination.
prop:topological-mass-formula-algebraic:
Proposition Topological mass formula (algebraic, \mathbb{Q}(q)-side). Let \beta \in H_n(R, q) be the Hecke normal form of a closed braid with \mathrm{Vol}_{q_0}(\beta) \neq 0. The categorical mass admits the closed form:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{alg}}(\beta)
  \;=\;
  \frac{\Phi_1(\beta)}{\hbar_q^{2}},
\qquad
  \Phi_1(\beta) \;=\; \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta)\bigr)
  \;=\; \ln\!\bigl\lvert\mathrm{Vol}_{q_0}(\beta)\bigr\rvert.

Before \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, the only object computed is \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta), which lies in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][(q^{2}+1)^{-1}] \subset \mathbb{Q}(q) at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). The absolute value and the logarithm are archimedean operations and are applied only after the specialisation q \mapsto q_0.

The algebraic quantum volume is a polynomial in z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) with coefficients in \mathbb{Z}[h] (cleared mass trace). Computing it needs no complex-analytic limit. Identifying \Phi_1 with the hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(K) is a separate step, and it rests on the volume conjecture (topological mass formula).
rem:residue-as-braid-holonomy:
Remark Each residue is the holonomy of a braid loop around a singular fibre. Each residue \mathrm{Res}_{q=\zeta_\ell}[\Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M,\,\ell}(T_w)] operates gauge-theoretically as the holonomy of the braid loop T_w around the singular fibre at q = \zeta_\ell.

The complex parameter q labels a flat holomorphic bundle of Hecke algebras over \mathbb{C}^\times. The algebra degenerates at roots of unity, creating singular fibres. The braid word defines a section that acquires monodromy when analytically continued around these fibres. The residue explicitly pairs this monodromy with the Markov trace.

At roots of unity, the Markov trace collapses to the Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant. The residues extract these invariants to populate the Habiro cyclotomic coefficients. For deep-strata braids, the regular-value tower converges too slowly; the holonomy residues supply the missing binding energy.
prop:graded-trace-residue-split:
Proposition Graded-trace residue split on the confinement filtration. The Markov trace decomposes canonically into smooth and oscillating components:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w, q_0)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{gr}}(T_w, q_0)
  \;+\;
  \mathrm{Res}_{\mathrm{GB}}(T_w, q_0).

The graded trace evaluates on the associated graded algebra, capturing the leading-order term. The residue sum tallies the rewriting defects from higher filtration strata via the Habiro expansion.

The split mirrors Strutinsky's macroscopic-plus-shell decomposition. The graded trace acts as the macroscopic liquid-drop baseline. The residue sum supplies the oscillating shell corrections.
rem:graded-trace-strutinsky-interpretati: Remark Strutinsky macroscopic-plus-shell reading of the graded-trace residue split. Physical interpretation of each piece. The categorical split maps onto the Strutinsky energy decomposition E = \tilde E + \delta E_{\mathrm{shell}}. The symbol map on the graded algebra implements the Strutinsky smoothing convolution. The residue sum recovers the sharp shell fluctuations that the smoothing procedure suppresses.
rem:term6-binding-density:
Remark Term 6 binding density: B(Z,N)/A \approx \alpha \cdot T_6(Z,N)/A^3 + \beta + \delta_M(Z,N). The nuclear binding energy per nucleon follows the structural decomposition:

  \frac{B(Z, N)}{A}
  \;\approx\;
  \alpha \cdot \frac{T_6(Z, N)}{A^3}
  \;+\;
  \beta
  \;+\;
  \delta_M(Z, N).

Here T_6 evaluates the level-3 Gröbner-Shirshov spectral-sequence stratum, while \alpha and \beta provide AME calibration constants.

The term T_6 enumerates ordered triples of nucleons, generating an intrinsic \sim A^3 scaling. Dividing by A^3 constructs the proper intensive density. The decomposition structure strictly derives from the spectral sequence and Hecke factorization, isolating the empirical inputs exclusively to the calibration scalars and operator-level magic-shell enhancements.

rem:delta-lambda-value-vs-magnitude:
Remark Per-partition \Delta_\lambda value versus open super-pairwise many-body binding magnitude. The partition weight \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda \in \mathbb{Z} established in DT/3d-index unification of \Delta_\lambda separates an exact combinatorial per-block value from an open many-body extensive binding magnitude. Following the Springer correspondence for a unipotent element of Jordan type \lambda in \mathrm{GL}_n, the top cohomology of the Springer fibre carries the irreducible S_n-module V_\lambda (Tonny A. Springer [springer1976]; Toshiaki Shoji [shoji2019, Thm. 2.1]), explaining the terminology while both the jet-valuation parity (-1)^{n(\lambda)} and the Wedderburn dimension \dim V_\lambda are derived directly within the Hecke substrate.

Intensive per-block value versus extensive many-body magnitude. Because the normalized Markov-trace weighted sum \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda(q)\,\chi^\lambda(\beta)\,\Delta_\lambda is intensive, no per-partition scalar weight \Delta_\lambda can generate the super-pairwise extensive nuclear binding energy documented in Term 6 binding density. Six distinct ansätze attempting to absorb the light-nuclide magnitude deficit (r^\ast \approx 1.585 at the deuteron) into \Delta_\lambda—Frobenius co-Casimir, Demazure-fibre, LP-Plancherel, LP-Frobenius, level-0 crystal-graph, and augmented-Markov—all fail at A = 2. Furthermore, the pairwise exchange determinant on [0, 1] satisfies (1 - m^2)^6 \le (1 + 3m)(1 - m)^3, capping the four-body pairwise log-determinant cumulant at \rho_4 \le \binom{4}{2} = 6, whereas nuclear {}^4\mathrm{He} binding requires \rho_4 \approx 13 > 6. Any genuine closure of the many-body binding magnitude must therefore arise from an irreducibly super-pairwise (\ge 3-body) extensive mechanism rather than a re-weighting of \Delta_\lambda.

Phenomenological depth-two recurrences are not derivations. Discrete depth-two q-difference recurrences w_{n+1} = a_0 w_n + r_{\mathrm{res}} w_{n-1} on the [n]_q!-normalized carrier (distinct up to scalar gauge from the resurgent Stokes carrier of Stavros Garoufalidis, Jie Gu, and Marcos Mariño [garoufalidis-gu-marino2021]) reproduce multi-body binding hierarchies only when seeded with calibrated phenomenological constants (a_0 = 1/2, r_{\mathrm{res}} \approx 2.596, and empirical isospin shifts). Under the three-observable calibration discipline (m_e, \mathfrak{D}_\beta, m_\pi), such seeded recurrences are exploratory fits rather than parameter-free predictions; the parameter-free many-body nuclear binding magnitude remains open.
rem:tjon-universality-external: Remark The external three-body/four-body correlation, and why it does not license the simplex baseline. The many-body magnitude leg of \Delta_\lambda (Per-partition \Delta_\lambda value versus open super-pairwise many-body binding magnitude) is scored against an external observable—the empirical correlation between three-body and four-body binding energies, known in nuclear physics as the Tjon line. Separating what the effective-field-theory literature establishes from the inclusion--exclusion simplex expansion prevents an analogy from being misread as a derived premise.
prop:habiro-residue-sum-equivalence:
Proposition Habiro completion ≡ Gröbner–Shirshov residue spectral sum (equivalence). Let T_w \in H_n(q) be a closed braid word and let \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w, q) denote its Markov trace, viewed in the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. The two formulations of \mathrm{tr}_M arising in this chapter agree on the archimedean realization

  \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \;\xrightarrow{\;\rho_\infty\;}\; \mathbb{R}

whenever both correspond to the same braid word T_w, namely:

  1. the polynomial-ring value, computed from any Habiro completion instance \mathcal{H} as \mathrm{eval}_{u_0}(\mathcal{H}.\mathrm{trace}) with u_0 = q_0^{1/2}, and

  2. the residue spectral sum, computed from any Gröbner–Shirshov residue spectral sum instance \mathcal{R} as \mathcal{R}.\mathrm{mass},

coincide as the two distinct constructions of \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) \in \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}.

This is a non-trivial analytic identity: it relates the cyclotomic-coefficient sum \sum_m a_m(u_0) \cdot (u_0;u_0)_m (Habiro side) to the residue-spectral-sum |\mathrm{tr}_M^{(0)}| + \sum_\ell \mathrm{Res}_{q\to\zeta_\ell}(\Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M,\ell}) (GB side). The analytic identification of the residue contributions with the cyclotomic tail remains open.

rem:habiro-residue-sum-equivalence-inter: Remark Constructive vs analytic handles on the same Habiro object. The polynomial-ring path is constructive (the Habiro coefficients a_m(u) are computed by sequential cyclotomic division, see Atomic-braid Habiro expansion: integrality and termination) while the residue path is analytic (it requires the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q and complex-analytic residues at primitive roots of unity). The equivalence shows the two viewpoints are two computational handles on the same underlying object in the Habiro ring, and lets later proofs use whichever is more tractable without losing rigour.
prop:borromean-h4-categorical-derivation:
Proposition Borromean h^4 = -3/4 derived as (-3) \cdot (1/4) via R-matrix + Markov normalisation. The h^4 coefficient of the Borromean Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = (4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6)/(h^2 + 4) factorises as

  \boxed{\;\;
  \bigl[h^4\text{-coeff of } \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})\bigr]
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{(-3)}_{\chi^{(2,1)}\text{ from R-matrix}}
  \;\cdot\;
  \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{4}}_{[2]_q^{-2}|_{q=1}\text{ Markov norm.}}
  \;=\;
  -\tfrac{3}{4},
  \;\;}

where -3 is the h^4 coefficient of the S_3 standard-irrep character \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 2 - 3h^4 - h^6, derived from the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) R-matrix on V_{1/2}^{\otimes 3} via Schur–Weyl duality; and 1/4 = 1/[2]_q^2|_{q=1} is the standard Markov-trace normalisation for c = 3-component link closure.

The connection to the wider framework and the significance of the factorisation are collected in the Borromean h^4 context.

Archimedean specialisation. The factor 1/4 = [2]_q^{-2}\big|_{q=1} is the archimedean q = 1 numerical evaluation of the exact Wenzl weight; the rational factorisation (-3)\cdot(1/4) = -3/4 holds over \mathbb{R}, on the archimedean side of the substrate wall.

prop:habiro-precision-ladder-equivalence:
Proposition Precision-ladder coefficients are Habiro integer evaluations. For a braid word T_w write u = q^{1/2} and \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w, q) = p_w(u)/d_w(u) in lowest terms, with p_w, d_w \in \mathbb{Z}[u]. The trace itself is not a polynomial in u: at z = q^3/(q^2+1), \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = z = u^6/(u^4+1). The denominator-cleared numerator p_w admits a finite Habiro expansion with integer coefficients,

  p_w(u) \;=\; \sum_{m=0}^{M} a_m(u) \cdot (u;\,u)_m,
  \qquad
  a_m \in \mathbb{Z}[u],
  \qquad M < \infty,

where (u;\,u)_m = \prod_{k=1}^{m}(1-u^{k}) is the q-Pochhammer symbol. It is an exact, finite rational evaluation, not a truncated series.

For the neutron–proton difference the expansion is applied to the numerator of \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_n) - \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_p) over a common denominator. Subtracting the two coefficient lists directly is not valid at z = q^3/(q^2+1), because the denominators differ: d_p = 4u^{18}(u^4+1)^2 and d_n = 4u^{18}.

Under the archimedean evaluation u \mapsto u_0 at the substrate square-root, each (u_0;\,u_0)_m with m \ll 1/(u_0 - 1) \approx 19 contributes a factor that shrinks like \sim \hbar_q^m, where \hbar_q is the universal substrate Planck quantum (categorical; the exact algebraic values at the substrate q_0 are not reproduced here).

The verified proton Habiro coefficients, the uniqueness of the archimedean evaluation, and the scope of the exact evaluation are collected in the Habiro precision-ladder context.

Archimedean specialisation. The Habiro / precision-ladder Taylor coefficients (\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}) are the real archimedean evaluations of the generic Habiro-ring expansion; the real coefficient sequences sit on the archimedean side of the substrate wall, acknowledged here.
prop:tau-M-asymptotic-rep-theory:
Proposition \mathrm{tr}_M^{V_\lambda}(\beta) = \mathrm{Tr}\,\rho_\lambda(\beta) \cdot \cos(\alpha_\lambda - b_\lambda\hbar_q^2/2) \cdot \prod_k(1 + c_k^{(\lambda)} u_\lambda^k): canonical u-ladder of the Markov-traced character. \mathrm{tr}_M ladder — representation-theoretic structure.

Proposition (conditional on the open recursion kernel of c_k precision-ladder recursion induced by the fibre-level Habiro q-difference equation; "\mathrm{tr}_M ladder").

For a typed braid \beta and a Hecke irreducible representation V_\lambda of H_n(q), the Markov-traced character at single wrap admits a canonical factorisation in the substrate ladder variable u_\lambda = b_\lambda\,\hbar_q^2 (where \hbar_q = (q-1)/q):

\boxed{
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{V_\lambda}(\beta)
   \;=\;
   \mathrm{Tr}\,\rho_\lambda(\beta) \cdot
   \cos\!\Bigl(\alpha_\lambda - \tfrac{b_\lambda \hbar_q^2}{2}\Bigr) \cdot
   \prod_{k \geq 2}\bigl(1 + c_k^{(\lambda)}\, u_\lambda^{\,k}\bigr),
}

This matches the canonical \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision ladder (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta categorical-derivation precision ladder), where:

  • \rho_\lambda is the Hoefsmit seminormal representation of H_n(q) on V_\lambda.
  • b_\lambda is the off-diagonal coupling of \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i) in the standard-tableau basis. For V_{(2,1)} of H_3, the scalar b = \sqrt{q^4+q^2+1}/(q^2+1) = \sqrt{d_1 d_2 + 1}.
  • \alpha_\lambda is the single-wrap eigenphase on V_\lambda. The \cos(\alpha_\lambda - b_\lambda\hbar_q^2/2) envelope carries the N=1 coupling b_\lambda.
  • c_k^{(\lambda)} are the rung coefficients of the ladder, representing the higher Ohtsuki invariants of the correction factor.

The factorisation defines the correction factor F_\lambda := \mathrm{tr}_M^{V_\lambda}(\beta) / \mathrm{Tr}\,\rho_\lambda(\beta), which is valid wherever \mathrm{Tr}\,\rho_\lambda(\beta) \neq 0. The right-hand side depends on \hbar_q only through \hbar_q^2, so the factorisation is even in \hbar_q by construction. This evenness is a property of the ansatz, not a consequence of the bar involution: under q \mapsto q^{-1} one has \hbar_q \mapsto 1 - q = -q\,\hbar_q, not -\hbar_q.

The rung coefficients are conjectured to be determined by the proved second-order q-difference (Hahn–Exton q-Bessel) recursion of c_k precision-ladder recursion induced by the fibre-level Habiro q-difference equation. The entire product forms the Taylor expansion of the exact finite Habiro sum, which the production system evaluates without truncation (Precision-ladder coefficients are Habiro integer evaluations).

prop:habiro-pochhammer-bridge:
Proposition Habiro–Markov bridge via Pochhammer factorisation. Let q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}, u = \sqrt{q}, and let \{a_m(u)\}_{m=0}^{M} be the Habiro coefficients of a braid word \beta \in B_n (integer polynomials in u). Define the two Pochhammer conventions:

  (q;q)_m \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{m}(1 - q^k),
  \qquad
  (u;u)_m \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{m}(1 - u^k).

Then 1 - q^k = (1 - u^k)(1 + u^k) for all k \geq 1, and the ratio of the two Habiro evaluations is the Habiro-weighted product:

  \frac{\sum_m a_m(u)\,(q;q)_m}{\sum_m a_m(u)\,(u;u)_m}
  \;=\;
  \Bigl\langle\prod_{k=1}^{m}(1 + u^k)\Bigr\rangle_{\!\mathrm{Hab}}

where the Habiro average is \langle f_m \rangle_{\mathrm{Hab}} = \sum_m a_m(u)\,(u;u)_m \cdot f_m \,/\, \sum_m a_m(u)\,(u;u)_m.
prf:habiro-pochhammer-bridge:
Proof Proof of habiro pochhammer bridge. The identity 1 - q^k = 1 - u^{2k} = (1 - u^k)(1 + u^k) is immediate from q = u^2. Applying it to each factor of the Pochhammer product gives

  (q;q)_m = \prod_{k=1}^{m}(1 - q^k)
  = \prod_{k=1}^{m}(1 - u^k)(1 + u^k)
  = (u;u)_m \cdot \prod_{k=1}^{m}(1 + u^k).

Substituting into the numerator:

  \sum_m a_m(u)\,(q;q)_m
  = \sum_m a_m(u)\,(u;u)_m \cdot \prod_{k=1}^{m}(1 + u^k).

Dividing by \sum_m a_m(u)\,(u;u)_m gives the weighted average. \square
prose:intro-cyclotomic-depth-3-trilog:
Arc II concludes at polylogarithmic depth 3. Whereas hyperbolic 3-manifold volumes reside at depth 2 in the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D(z) = \operatorname{Im}\mathrm{Li}_2(z), the sub-leading curvature and three-body holonomy invariants on Bring's surface evaluate to the depth-3 trilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_3(z) and the Clausen function \mathrm{Cl}_3(\theta) at fifth roots of unity \zeta_5.

This section establishes the depth-3 cyclotomic identities of the mass tower: the Tate-rationality of the imaginary part of \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5) via Jonquière's inversion relation, the explicit \mathrm{Cl}_3(\zeta_5) Galois orbit-sum identity and its PSLQ linear-independence verification, and the all-depth cyclotomic dimension synthesis. The section closes with the cyclotomic polynomial doubling identity \Phi_8(X) = \Phi_4(X^2) and its specialization to the level-2 \mathrm{SU}(2) Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev partition function at \zeta_8.
prop:bring-trilog-imaginary-tate-rationa:
Proposition Trilogarithm imaginary part at \zeta_5: Tate-rational closed form 4\pi^3/125 via Kummer reflection (50-dps verified). The imaginary part of the Bring trilog at \zeta_5 evaluates as:

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5)
  \;=\;
  S_3\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)
  \;=\;
  \frac{4 \pi^3}{125}.

Because 4\pi^3/125 lies in (2\pi i)^3 \cdot \mathbb{Q}, it is Tate-rational. It projects to zero under the Beilinson regulator quotient \mathcal{P}_3 \to \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathrm{Tate}.

This proposition halves the depth-3 unproved surface. The imaginary part resolves to a known rational multiple of \pi^3. The Borel-predicted 2-dimensional regulator image is generated entirely by the real parts \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) and \mathrm{Cl}_3(4\pi/5). The real part \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) stands alone as the genuinely new depth-3 period.
